options.plain: Tablets at home and an infusion, over three months
options.benefit: Shorter course; fewer weeks of treatment.
options.burden: Tablets need careful daily management; bowel and hand/foot symptoms can occur.

options.plain: Infusions with a take-home pump, over six months
options.benefit: Another way to deliver treatment; avoids daily chemotherapy tablets.
options.burden: Longer course, pump care and more visits; persistent tingling may limit walking.

options.plain: No additional chemotherapy after surgery; continue follow-up and supportive care
options.benefit: Avoids chemotherapy-related toxicity and infusion visits.
options.burden: Foregoes possible chemotherapy benefit; cancer may still return. Follow-up and symptom care continue.

sideEffectReference.title: Bijwerkingen bij kanker · side-effect topics
sideEffectReference.limitation: Topic selection based on the side-effect index returned by web search. Direct page retrieval unavailable; regimen-specific advice and frequencies not verified. Definitions below are our plain-language summaries, not quotations.

sideEffects.name: Hair loss
sideEffects.description: Some cancer treatments can cause hair thinning or loss. Whether it occurs depends on the treatment; it is not assumed for every regimen.

sideEffects.name: Neuropathy
sideEffects.description: Treatment-related nerve symptoms can include tingling, numbness or pain in hands or feet and may affect daily activities.

sideEffects.name: Fatigue
sideEffects.description: Cancer and its treatment can cause tiredness that affects daily activity. It is not always relieved by rest.

sideEffects.name: Nausea and vomiting
sideEffects.description: Cancer treatment can make a person feel sick or vomit. The clinical team should assess symptoms and discuss supportive care.

sideEffects.name: Hand–foot syndrome
sideEffects.description: Some treatments can cause sore, red or peeling skin on palms and soles. This differs from nerve damage (neuropathy).

terms.Adjuvant therapy: Extra treatment after surgery to reduce the chance that cancer returns. It does not mean cancer is known to remain.
terms.Resection: An operation to remove the part of the bowel containing the cancer.
terms.Neuropathy: Numbness, tingling or pain from affected nerves, often in hands or feet. It can make walking or using your hands harder.
